content.comment_body: Hello, I am new to [company_name] PLCs and could use some guidance. I have a project file I want to upload to my PLC ([article_no]), but I get an error saying it’s incompatible because it was created with the default hardware settings ([product_name] [version_no]). Is there a way to change the hardware type so I can upload my program without starting over? I've attached my program and hardware type options as reference. I appreciate any assistance.

It looks like your [product_name] file is corrupted, and it may not be the original project file. All blocks appear to be copied from another [product_name] file. For example, Block B005 has the name B46, Block B069 is named B27, etc. When I try changing the hardware type to [article_no], I get an error message, but the diagram shows no AI1. If I copy all blocks to a new blank diagram, that error disappears, and it’s possible to change the hardware type to a different version ([article_no]), but not to [article_no]. Edit: I created a new diagram, set the hardware to [article_no], and that worked. However, copying blocks from your file into the new diagram doesn’t work — I receive the same message when trying to change the hardware type.

That’s interesting, I’m not seeing those error messages on my end. The project wasn’t made for [product_name] [version_no] either, as more text modules have been used than that version supports, and not in the correct format. You'll probably need to rewrite your project for the [product_name] [version_no]. Kind regards, [user_name] (translated with Google)

As previously mentioned, the [product_name] file is corrupted. You'll need to rewrite the entire diagram. Start by creating a new blank diagram and set the hardware type to [article_no] before programming. Also, you don’t need to use just one sheet per diagram; you can add multiple horizontal and vertical sheets. Use the button in the menu for this.

Alternatively, you can copy the program into a new one set to [article_no], but you’ll first have to delete all text modules and recreate them. Note that only 10 text blocks are available for [product_name] [version_no], so you’ll need to leave some out (I did the first step, but the text modules need to be inserted by you). Kind regards, [user_name]
Also be aware: The message text in [article_no] is limited to 4 lines instead of 6, and only 12 characters per line instead of 16.
Thank you very much for your assistance. The issue was resolved by removing the text boxes and recreating them in the [product_name] [version_no] program.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter compatibility problems when transferring project files created for newer [product_name] hardware to older versions due to differences in structure and supported features such as block format and text module limits. These software restrictions on hardware type changes often result in confusing error messages and situations where project files may be corrupted or damaged, forcing users to manually rewrite or modify their projects.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate that they can easily switch hardware types within the software and upload projects to older hardware versions without needing to completely rewrite their diagrams.
